_provenance.written_by: manual sweep against the operator's real project tree, re-measured 2026-08-16 after the round-two oracle fix
_provenance.dod_line: the liveness oracle's classification equivalence observed on the operator's real project tree
_provenance.supersedes: the 2026-08-16 first run, which measured the ROUND-ONE oracle — a module with a two-valued `exists` seam and first-match-wins over the collision class. Those numbers described code that no longer exists and were replaced rather than kept alongside, because two sets of figures for one file is how a stale one gets cited.
_provenance.how_to_reproduce: run classifyProjects and the consumer's classifyDirectory over ~/.theokit/projects and compare verdict by verdict. The script must run from the TheoCode repo (its tsconfig paths resolve the consumer oracle's single import, `encodeProjectDir` from `@theokit/agents/persistence`) AND as ESM — a `.ts` file in a directory without `type: module` is resolved as CJS, and the `./persistence` subpath has no `require` condition, which fails with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED and looks like a missing export rather than a resolution mode.
honest_limits: This is a MANUAL sweep, not integration-test infra. The file is hand-written from a measured run; no test writes it. A future run must re-measure rather than trust this file.

The consumer additionally does a DFS from / for projects with no transcript, which the framework cannot do without an injected pool. All 5 disagreements are that asymmetry, and every one of them is the framework being LESS certain, never more.
The tree measured is one machine's. The scale-independent property (ops <= budget) holds at any size; the agreement percentage is about this tree.

One project moved from (framework undetermined, consumer ALIVE) to (framework undetermined, consumer UNDETERMINED) between the two runs. That is the CONSUMER's verdict changing on a tree that drifted during the session, not an effect of the fix — recorded rather than smoothed over.

_the_property_that_matters: framework_dead_where_consumer_disagreed == 0. The caller DELETES on `dead`; a false `dead` is data loss and a false `undetermined` is a directory left on disk. The two errors are not symmetric, so the only agreement number that carries safety weight is this one.
_candidate_pool_arm: The sweep ran twice on the same tree: once with an EMPTY candidate pool and once with a REALISTIC one (1425 real absolute paths, two levels under ~/Projetos and ~). Both arms produced identical verdicts and identical fs operation counts (34640), because `searchPool` filters candidates by string encoding BEFORE probing — a non-matching candidate costs CPU, not a filesystem call — and on this tree no candidate matched any of the 3363 projects that reach the fall-through. Wall clock rose 430ms to 1777ms, which is what confirms the loop ran rather than being skipped. The honest reading: on this machine the recorded-cwd read carries the entire result and the pool contributes nothing. That is the measured case for the fix's direction (the answer, not the search), not an argument that `candidatePaths` is dead — a machine whose projects moved would exercise it.
_budget_sizing_finding: A first run at budget=20000 exhausted it exactly (framework_ops == 20000) and agreement fell to 66.2%, because 7967 projects degraded to `undetermined` for want of budget rather than for want of evidence. That degradation is SAFE (nothing is deleted) but SILENT: the sweep does almost nothing and no aggregate signal says why. At the measured 2.54 ops/project, a tree of N projects needs budget >= 3N. Nothing in the module warns when the budget is undersized for the input — filed as a follow-up.
